newsitem.title: GERMANY: Key Kohl aide says Bonn coalition not in danger.
newsitem.headline: Key Kohl aide says Bonn coalition not in danger.

text.p: A chief aide to German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Monday the centre-right coalition of Christian Democrats (CDU) and Free Democrats (FDP) was not in danger despite a lingering row over taxes.

Wolfgang Schaeuble, the CDU whip in the lower house of parliament and most widely tipped as Kohl's successor, said the coalition had a number of serious problems to overcome but that these could be resolved within a few weeks.

Schaeuble told reporters after a meeting of the parliamentary group of Kohl's alliance of CDU and Bavarian sister party Christian Social Union (CSU) that the coalition's lower house majority would pass tax legislation this week.
The lower house would also overturn the rejection of health reform legislation by the upper house, which is controlled by the opposition Social Democrats (SPD).

Schaeuble said the CDU/CSU parliamentary group did not discuss the current dispute with coalition partner FDP over how to plug the widening budget deficit because Finance Minister Theo Waigel was not present at the meeting.
Waigel was attending a meeting of European Union economic and finance ministers in Luxembourg.
